raw.title: The Threepenny Opera
raw.extract: The Threepenny Opera is a 1928 German "play with music." Kurt Weill wrote the music, while the libretto by Bertolt Brecht and Elisabeth Hauptmann was adapted from Hauptmann's translation of John Gay's 18th-century English ballad opera The Beggar's Opera. The libretto also incorporates four ballads by François Villon. Although the first edition of the work credits Hauptmann only as the translator of the source material, in 1955 Brecht acknowledged that she had been had been a full partner in the creation of the play, stating that "The ongoing work with Weill and Elisabeth Hauptmann was a true collaboration that progressed step by step."
